comparator.name: Bachelor Biomedical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 Biomedical Engineering after-revision PER Articles 3.3–3.5 and Appendix 2, and generation-2026 chart (2026–2027, 2027–2028, 2028–2029), were freshly retrieved and inspected on 8 October 2026. Instruction is Dutch and English, correcting normalized ENG-only metadata while preserving raw ENG provenance. This is the BBT Biomedical Engineering programme, not the alternative MWT Medical Sciences and Technology core. Current core 125 EC includes 110 taught/project EC and 8FINAL Bachelor Final Project 15; ITEC is 10 and genuine free space 45, replacing the older 105/15/15/45 allocation. Year one is 55 core + 5 ITEC (60); year two 40 core + 20 electives (60); year three 15 taught core + 5 ITEC + 15 project + 25 electives (60). Skills Experience 8BA050 spans two 5-EC quarter positions and is counted once at 10 EC. Personal and Professional Development is embedded in existing core/CBL credits; mandatory MyFuture activities and five Studium Generale activities for ITEC carry no separately added credit here. The 45 free EC require at least 30 EC at levels 2/3, including at least 15 at level 3; external courses require approval and degree-content overlap must be avoided. Pink diagram examples are recommendations; MWT-only core such as Mechanobiology and Cancer Cell Biology is not added as universal BBT formation. Required BBT Materials Science remains included. For 8BA020, the current cohort diagram and official TU/e course profile use Engineering organs on a chip; the formal PER uses Engineering a Tissue. The component retains this title variation explicitly at the same code, required CBL role and 5 EC, without asserting a formal PER amendment. NAC 8BB070 is retained without an unsupported acronym expansion. BEP admission requires at least 120 completed credits including compulsory first-year components, all year-one/two P&PD skills, eight year-two/three core units including two year-two CBLs, and four year-two/three elective units. Results in the immediately preceding examination period do not count for this entry check, and interim results do not count for a Q1 start. The interdisciplinary challenge requires prior participation in the offered units embedding communication, cooperation, planning and organizing (8BA020/8BA050). No duplicate skills, route alternatives or optional biomedical examples adds credits.

core: Human biology, cells, biomolecules, physiology and experimental life science
Mathematical and computational modelling of biological and technical systems
Medical imaging and biomedical signal/image analysis
Statistics and machine learning for biomedical measurements
Patient-oriented healthcare technology and design projects
adjacent: Disease mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment and clinical translation

trace: develops customer-led product concepts, fabrication methods, prototypes, quantitative models and sustainability/cost analysis; this supports patient-oriented design work without claiming medical-device engineering
implements search, constraint satisfaction and optimisation for complex biomedical-model and design problems
develops algorithm and data-structure design with performance analysis for reproducible biomedical-data workflows
provides data cleaning, manipulation, visualisation and project work for interpreting biomedical measurements
applies regression and tree-based learning to real data, including documented medical examples
directly studies image feature detection, tracking and medical-image applications; it does not supply image-acquisition physics
develops neural-network and computer-vision models for advanced biomedical image/data analysis
studies kinematics, motion planning and robotic manipulation as computational foundations for assistive or clinical systems, not biomedical hardware
supplies structured programming, testing and debugging for scientific computation and biomedical-data analysis
establishes calculus, vectors, matrices and differential equations for physiological and technical models
develops matrix methods, linear transformations and eigenvalue reasoning for multivariable biomedical models
implements numerical equation solving, integration and differential equations for dynamic physiological models
extends calculus to several variables and differential equations for coupled biological processes
studies differential-equation, transfer-function and state-space representations relevant to physiological signals and systems
develops probability, estimation and simulation for biomedical measurements and model uncertainty
studies human structure/function through imaging, surface anatomy and dissection materials
connects molecular drug targets and kinetics to therapeutic effects and toxicity
studies immune recognition, host-pathogen interactions, inflammation and tissue damage
investigates molecular and cellular defects causing pathology and their treatment across organ systems
introduces macromolecules, cells, DNA, organ systems and health/disease as the biological foundation
introduces brain anatomy, injury and behaviour as a defined human-system application
directly studies prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell biology, current research and reproducibility
studies human structure/function, signalling, homeostasis, energy handling and integrated organ systems
studies biomolecule chemistry, metabolic pathways and their roles in health and disease
practises biochemical and molecular laboratory work with blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics
studies mutations, genetic testing, cell injury, inflammation, repair and neoplasia
adds regression, multivariate inference, experimental design and applied analysis for biomedical research
develops systematic review, meta-analysis, effect-size calculation and bias assessment for evidence-based health research

alternatives.label: Biomedical imaging, modelling & data systems
alternatives.concept: Combine human biology and laboratory science with mathematical systems, programming, statistics, machine learning, medical-image analysis, computational robotics and product design. This is a biomedical-data and systems response, not a biomedical-device engineering substitute.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule contains a cumulative biology/laboratory sequence and a cumulative mathematical, computational, imaging and design sequence; the label avoids claiming the absent mechanics, electronics and instrumentation formation.
progression: All exact Fall 2026-start availability and recorded formal prerequisites pass. Life, health and biomedicine precedes all dependent life-science and biomedical courses; Brain & Behavior precedes Advanced Research Seminar in the disease alternative. Mathematical Methods precedes all dependent mathematics, Robotics and neural-network study. Programming precedes Algorithms and optimisation. The schedules contain exactly 24 courses, four per semester, Year-1 PPD and six 300-level courses each.

alternatives.label: Human physiology, molecular disease & quantitative health
alternatives.concept: Retain human biology, laboratory work, physiology, mathematical models, statistics and medical-image analysis while prioritising pharmacology, immunity, disease mechanisms and evidence synthesis for diagnosis and treatment questions.
alternatives.labelReason: Five advanced computational courses are replaced by pharmacology, immunology, disease mechanisms, brain/behaviour foundations and health-evidence synthesis, producing a distinct biomedical-science route without a clinical or engineering claim.
progression: All exact Fall 2026-start availability and recorded formal prerequisites pass. Life, health and biomedicine precedes all dependent life-science and biomedical courses; Brain & Behavior precedes Advanced Research Seminar in the disease alternative. Mathematical Methods precedes all dependent mathematics, Robotics and neural-network study. Programming precedes Algorithms and optimisation. The schedules contain exactly 24 courses, four per semester, Year-1 PPD and six 300-level courses each.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. Algorithms, Robotics, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Optimisation and Deep Learning are replaced by Pharmacology, Infection & Immunity, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Mechanisms of Disease and Advanced Research Seminar.

candidates.label: Physiology, disease mechanisms and clinical translation
Medical devices, biomechanics and tissue engineering

selection.assessment: Two complete related programmes pass the content, schedule and 30-EC distinctness gates. The first owns the integrated imaging/modelling/data direction; the second is independently supported by physiology, diagnosis, treatment and clinical-translation interests. A further device, biomechanics and tissue-engineering direction cannot supply tissue mechanics, biomaterials, sensors, circuits, instrumentation, clinical measurement hardware or tissue-engineering laboratories. General anatomy, robotics and product design cannot be relabelled as those subjects. No third programme is manufactured.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives combine biomedical science, laboratory work, quantitative modelling, image/data analysis and design, with either computational systems or molecular disease applications. They do not reproduce the target's physics, tissue mechanics, flow/diffusion, biomaterials, sensors, electronics, instrumentation, engineering projects or biomedical capstone.
